title: Estimating by rounding
keyIdea: Round each number to a nearby ten, then calculate. The result is an estimate — close and quick, not always exact.
familyTip: At the shop, round prices to the nearest 10p or £1 and add. Compare with the till total: was your estimate a bit low or high?

visual.caption: Rounding & estimates — fair idea or myth? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: an estimate must equal the exact answer
always round down to be safe

lab.caption: Flagship lab: round on a number line, midpoint-5 rule, estimate a sum, judge low vs high, reject always-round-down, then challenge.

kid: Rounding finds a nearby ten that is easy to use.
If the ones digit is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, round down.
To estimate a sum, round each number, then add.
An estimate is close and quick. It does not have to match the exact answer.
adult: NC Y3 / CCSS 3.NBT.A.1: round whole numbers to the nearest 10; use rounding to estimate sums. Words: round, nearest ten, estimate, midpoint, ones digit.
Common mistakes: always rounding down; thinking the estimate must equal the exact sum; leaving 5 as-is instead of rounding up; rounding only one addend.
In the lab your child rounds 27→30 and 25→30, estimates 28+34 as 60, sees that 60 is a bit low versus 62, and states the 5-up rule.
